newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers dip, but Med prices march up.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers dip, but Med prices march up.

text.p: ARA bunker prices dipped on Wednesday, while Mediterranean prices rose in response to ARA and general crude strength earlier this week, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 cst was down $1/$2 a tonne to $124/$126 fob as weekly builds in refined product stocks in the United States weakened crude.
In ARA itself, product appeared relatively tight. One major had sold out for the entire week, while another was reported to be having short-term loading difficulties.
After a modest rush of buying on Tuesday, shipowners were quiet, enquiries being less than 10,000 tonnes.
Hamburg bunkers were little changed and demand was extremely poor.
Mediterranean prices were steady to firm. Bunkers from Spanish ports were about $2 a tonne higher. However, the prospect of lower prices on Thursday deterred any buying interest.
In Fujairah prices weakened by $2/$3, although there were signs of improving demand.
Saudi Aramco, meanwhile, decided to keep fuel oil bunkers in the Gulf and the Red Sea at $127 a tonne.
